prediction_question: For a Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) telemetric river-level station in Malaysia, will the station's water level exceed its official published Danger threshold at any hourly reading within the next 24 hours, given the station's own water-level and rainfall history through hour H?
prediction_time: Hour H of day D: hourly telemetry through H is knowable, and no reading after H exists. Features are the station's own trailing level/rainfall statistics; every reading in (H, H+24] is label source and never ships as a feature.
target_definition: Binary: any hourly water-level reading for the station in (H, H+24] strictly above the station's published Danger Level (m). The thresholds are official per-station values shown on the publisher's per-state river pages (Normal/Alert/Warning/Danger columns, measured present in the fetched HTML), not chosen by us. Label source = the future level series; ships only as the binary label.

license_evidence: Measured 2026-10-20: no licence, copyright or terms text appears anywhere in the fetched portal HTML (home page 93,377 bytes, KEL state river page 76,926 bytes, trend page 190,352 bytes - grepped for copyright/hak cipta/terms/privacy). The publisher displays data publicly and states the system's purpose (public flood information), but display is not redistribution; per the standing rule the licence is recorded as an open question, not assumed.

Measured 2026-10-28 on the redesigned portal: still no licence, copyright or terms text anywhere in the fetched HTML (home, /waterlevel, /rainfall, Kelantan state page grepped for copyright/hak cipta/terms/syarat/privacy/privasi/lesen/license; only a 'Privasi' privacy link). The telemetry is absent from the data.gov.my CC BY 4.0 catalogue (355 datasets enumerated), so no national open-data licence covers it; the historical archive is application-gated (SPRHIN). Posture: publisher silent on redistribution = class C leaning; no operator risk acceptance exists for this candidate, and the standing policy forbids inventing one.

measurements.current_pages_2026_10_20: State river page /aras-air/data-paras-air/?state=KEL&lang=en: HTTP 200, 76,926 bytes, per-station rows carrying Normal/Alert/Warning/Danger threshold columns ('Danger Level:', 'Warning Level:', 'Alert Level:', 'Normal Level.' measured in HTML); 15 state options enumerated (PLS Kedah through WLP Labuan). The portal describes nearly 200 hydrological stations with real-time telemetry.
measurements.trend_endpoints_2026_10_20: Trend page JS (lines 1300/1409/2752/3327 of the fetched HTML) issues the four anonymous AJAX endpoints listed in sources; all answered HTTP 200.
measurements.historical_probe_failure_2026_10_20: The 1-hour endpoint answers 'Tiada data / No data' for state=KEL with placeholder district/station values; the water-level DT endpoint answers '{"count":,]}No result' for a station code taken from the state page (CC2127) across four date formats (2026-07-01/2026-07-03 and 01/07/2026/03/07/2026, datafreq=60). Endpoints are alive and anonymous, but the district/station keys and date format the frontend actually sends were not captured. The dropdown helpers return only the 'ALL' placeholder for the values tried, and a third-party-documented live-feed path (latestreadingstrendabc.json) 404s at three guessed locations.
measurements.api_contract_2026_10_28: Portal redesigned between 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-28: old WordPress trend AJAX endpoints now 404 (searchresultwaterleveldtlead_rptdb.php measured 404 for both station key formats; searchdistricttrend.php serves only a 'Notis Gangguan' maintenance image), so the recorded unpark step 1 is obsolete. New anonymous JSON API (Laravel) with a public bearer token embedded in every portal page HTML: POST /api/detailstation {state,district,station_name,parameter} returns per station: station_id, station_name, district, basins, last_update, water_level, official normal/alert/warning/danger thresholds, trend, wl_severity, graph_url. The official Danger Level (label threshold) is served per station by the publisher itself.
measurements.history_window_2026_10_28: The only historical series on the public web is the per-station graph endpoint https://infobanjirjps<state>.water.gov.my/WaterLevel/GetWaterLevelGraph/<id>: measured for station 101 (Sg. Kelantan di Jambatan Tendong): 95,195 bytes, 2,068 points at 5-min cadence covering EXACTLY the trailing 7 days (2026-10-21T00:00 -> 2026-10-28T04:15); startDate/endDate and from/to params are ignored (same 7-day window measured twice). No multi-year history is anonymously obtainable any more.
measurements.national_cost_2026_10_28: National extraction cost measured from the coordinator (probe/poll_states.py, 15 state requests, 2026-10-28): 563 water-level stations, 241,534 bytes, 43.6 s total. Largest states: Sarawak 121 stations/51,099 B, Selangor 86, Johor 58, Kedah 50. A daily collection poll is ~0.25 MB/day.
measurements.history_paths_closed_2026_10_28: (a) data.gov.my catalogue enumerated: 355 datasets (storage.data.gov.my/metrics/dataset_list.csv), NO river-level telemetry (closest: water_pollution_basin, yearly aggregate pollution classes) - the CC BY 4.0 posture measured for PriceCatcher does not carry to this telemetry. (b) archive.data.gov.my (holds the official aras-air-sungai-malaysia.csv threshold table per search index) unreachable from the coordinator: connection timeout, HTTP 000 (25 s and 60 s attempts) - access failure, not absence. (c) mywater.gov.my Telemetri module = station inventory with Excel export only; historical series are application-gated via SPRHIN (sprhin.water.gov.my; free for government/academic use, charged for private, approval required - JPS FAQ measured on jpsweb.terengganu.gov.my and mywater.gov.my). (d) InaTEWS-style feed alternatives: none for MY river levels.

rejection_reason: PARK (status parked), re-evaluated 2026-10-28. The original blocker (XHR parameter contract unknown) is RESOLVED-OBSOLETE: the portal was redesigned and the old WordPress endpoints are gone; the new JSON API is documented and anonymous. The blocker is now decisive and different: NO multi-year history is anonymously obtainable (per-station graphs serve a 7-day rolling window only; date params ignored; data.gov.my carries no river telemetry; archive.data.gov.my unreachable from the coordinator; MyWater exposes only a station inventory; the historical archive is application-gated via SPRHIN). The licence remains unresolved (no terms on the portal; absent from the national open-data catalogue; no operator risk acceptance exists). The retrospective multi-year panel this record originally imagined is therefore NOT buildable anonymously. The only viable design is a forward-collection cohort (daily polls accumulating a station-hour panel; northeast monsoon Nov-Mar generates positives), which requires BOTH an operator infrastructure decision AND a licence resolution before publication. Prior-art position unchanged: no packaged official-threshold exceedance classification task on this publisher's telemetry was found (Caravan = discharge regression; Google Flood Hub = operational forecasts; FloodCastBench = coastal).
next_action: Operator decision required to unpark (two decisions, in order): (1) authorize a forward-collection loop on the public API - one scheduled daily job polling POST /api/detailstation per state plus per-station GetWaterLevelGraph (measured cost 563 stations / ~0.25 MB / <1 min per day; probe/poll_states.py is the recipe), accumulating a station-hour panel whose label is any (H, H+24] reading above the official Danger Level - starting before the Nov-Mar monsoon captures the first positive season; (2) resolve the licence before any publication: publisher terms, or an explicit candidate-specific operator risk acceptance (the portal is silent; the telemetry is absent from the data.gov.my CC BY 4.0 catalogue; SPRHIN is application-gated). Absent (1)+(2), this stays parked. Reopen triggers: operator authorization; the portal or data.gov.my publishing redistribution terms; or the telemetry appearing in the data.gov.my catalogue.
